extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary officials, and legal professionals subject to USPTO regulation
extracted.subtask_description: A formal Final Order resolving disciplinary action against a registered practitioner for neglecting client matters and violating USPTO professional conduct rules, setting out stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions and procedures for reinstatement and publication. Useful as a template or precedent for sanctions and remedial requirements in USPTO disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and applicability of USPTO professional rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is registered to practice before the Office in patent matters (Reg. No. 37,169) and is subject to the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.20-10.112) for conduct prior to May 3, 2013 and the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101-11.901) effective May 3, 2013. The USPTO Director has jurisdiction pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that registered practitioners are governed by these specific regulatory provisions and that the Director has statutory and regulatory authority to adjudicate disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify clients of USPTO correspondence (Office Actions and Notices of Abandonment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent failed to notify his clients about multiple Office Actions received from the USPTO and failed to notify clients about Notices of Abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order treats failure to notify clients of correspondence from the USPTO as professional misconduct; practitioners must notify clients of Office Actions and abandonment notices to avoid violation of the Rules/Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to avoid neglect and not allow client applications to be abandoned without consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent, by act or omission, allowed at least 13 U.S. Patent Applications to become abandoned without the consent of his clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglecting entrusted patent applications and allowing abandonment without client consent constitutes grounds for discipline under the USPTO professional rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of cited regulatory provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b) via 10.23(c)(8); 10.77(c); 11.103; and 11.104(a)(2) and (3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cited provisions are the legal basis for the disciplinary findings; the Final Order ties the factual misconduct (failure to notify, neglect, abandonment) directly to these specific regulatory violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of mitigating and aggravating factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent expressed remorse, initiated restitution to clients (including paying USPTO fees and not billing for services), implemented a new docketing system, had no prior USPTO discipline, attributed some misconduct to caring for an ill father, and proposed associating with other practitioners upon reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanction decisions consider contrition, corrective actions, absence of prior discipline, personal circumstances, and planned remedial measures as mitigating factors; these factors are explicitly listed as 'Additional Considerations' informing the agreed sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension from practice (length and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters for ninety (90) days commencing on the date the Final Order is signed, and shall remain suspended until the OED Director grants a petition reinstating Respondent pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies both a fixed suspension term (90 days) and the procedural condition that suspension continues until successful reinstatement per regulatory petition procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with specific reinstatement and resignation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates adherence to the regulatory procedures governing resignation/withdrawal (11.58) and reinstatement (11.60) as conditions of the Final Order and any future petition to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing Legal Education requirement (practice management)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall complete at least five (5) credit hours of Continuing Legal Education covering law office practice management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes an education requirement targeted at practice management as a remedial step to reduce future neglect; specifies minimum credit hours and subject area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation period and enforcement procedure upon reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon reinstatement, Respondent shall serve a two (2) year probationary period commencing on the date of his reinstatement. If the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply during the probationary period, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to Respondent's address of record, grant fifteen (15) days to respond, and may request the USPTO Director to immediately suspend Respondent for up to an additional twenty-one (21) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details stepwise enforcement: issuance and service of an Order to Show Cause, a 15-day response window, evidentiary submission to the USPTO Director, and potential additional suspension up to 21 months; clarifies procedural rights and consequences during probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and Public Key Infrastructure ("PKI") certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative security measure to ensure suspended practitioners cannot access USPTO electronic services; a routine part of suspension orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on applying for or obtaining a USPTO Customer Number while suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents circumvention of suspension by obtaining new electronic access credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice of suspension text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates public disclosure of the Final Order and a standardized Official Gazette notice summarizing the misconduct, violations, sanctions, and mitigating information; serves both transparency and public protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding in future complaints or disciplinary proceedings involving Respondent, including as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements, and when considering any request for reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Makes explicit that the record may be used in subsequent enforcement or reinstatement contexts and may weigh against Respondent in future matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that no party will recover costs from the other as part of this settlement.
